siblingFile: api-data/cdm-connectors-state.json — GET /p0/cdm/connectors/state (all seven rollups) and GET /p0/cdm/connectors/{connector}/state (one rollup + taxonomy groups), both derived from this same flow_state table. Consume together: rollup for tab status/counts, this for file names, duplicate detection and the per-file grid.

auth.note: Handled globally by src/proxy.js + src/app/api/_lib/proxy.js. Never add auth headers per-route. A missing session is a 401 with a STRING `detail` ({"detail": "Missing session"}), raised by middleware BEFORE routing — so an unauthenticated call to a path that does not exist is indistinguishable from one to a path that does.

notes: 2026-08-17: first live sample shared (plant DELTA_CAPTURE, flow=gloc). One row per FILE.

2026-08-18 CONTRACT UPDATE — five changes, three of them breaking-ish. (1) `flow` is now VALIDATED: an unknown value used to be HTTP 200 + empty list, indistinguishable from a plant with no data; it is now a 422. It is also case-insensitive and trimmed, and echoed back normalised. (2) NEW `lifecycle` query param — the processed/unprocessed split, computed SERVER-side so the UI never derives it. (3) `status` as a QUERY PARAM is DEPRECATED, kept as an alias for lifecycle; sending both with disagreeing values is a 422. (4) An unknown `status` used to silently DISABLE the filter and return every row while echoing the bad value back — now rejected. (5) FOUR new endpoints: GET /flow/state/{flowUid}, POST /flow/upsert, POST /flow/{flowUid}/reset, DELETE /flow/{flowUid}.

2026-08-18 RESOLVED (was the file's top open issue): `flow` is OPTIONAL. Omit it and every flow for the plant comes back in ONE response with `data.flow === null`. This is what let the frontend delete its eight-way per-flow fan-out — see fetchStrategy below. NOTE `flow=` (present but blank) is NOT the same as omitting it: a blank value is a 422.

IMPORTANT — `flow` is the FLOW name, not the connector name. EIGHT flows vs SEVEN connectors. Only two connectors differ: `documents` → flow `docs`, and `timeseries` → flows ['ts','ts_values'] (TWO flows for one connector, which is exactly why connector names cannot be aliased — aliasing would have to silently pick one and drop the other). The other five (pnid, sap, aif, gloc, lopc) match their connector name exactly. Passing a connector name is a 422 whose message names the flow(s) to use AND points at /connectors/{connector}/state.

FOUR overlapping vocabularies, two of which are both called `status`. Do not conflate them: (a) `lifecycle` — the QUERY FILTER: pending|processed|failed|all, derived server-side from stage+status, stored nowhere; (b) `status` — the ROW field: pending|running|done|ok|failed|skipped, the OUTCOME of the last operation; (c) `stage` — the ROW field: uploaded|staged|processing|processed|reviewing|reviewed|committing|committed|superseded, WHERE the file is in the pipeline, and what lifecycle is derived from; (d) connector `status` — UPPERCASE, on /connectors/{connector}/state, a rollup of the highest-rank state across every file. `pending` appears in both (a) and (b) and means DIFFERENT things — as a filter it is 'not yet through extraction', as a row value it is 'reset, awaiting reprocess'. Only `failed` means the same in both.

HOW lifecycle IS DERIVED (mirrored in deriveFileLifecycle in src/components/admin/connectorState.js): `failed` is checked FIRST — status=='failed' at ANY stage, so a committed file that failed is 'failed', not 'processed'. Then `processed` = status!='failed' AND stage ∈ {processed, reviewing, reviewed, committing, committed}. Then `pending` = everything else, i.e. stage ∈ {uploaded, staged, processing, superseded}. ⚠ `processing` and `superseded` BOTH count as pending — a file mid-processing is reported pending, not processed. For a separate in-progress badge read stage=='processing' directly.

2026-08-18 BUG THIS CONTRACT EXPOSED IN OUR CODE (now fixed): connectorState.js's PROCESSED_STAGES was ['processed','reviewed','committed','ingested'] — it MISSED `reviewing` and `committing` (so every file in those two transient stages read as unprocessed: stale Unprocessed badge, and getUnprocessedTypes offering an already-extracted file for reprocessing) and contained `ingested`, which is not a stage at all.

`duplicate_of` CAN EQUAL THE ROW'S OWN flow_uid — confirmed in the captured response (flow_uid 51 carries duplicate_of 51). Treat `duplicate_of === flow_uid` as 'NOT a duplicate' rather than rendering a self-referencing badge. Always read it through duplicateSourceUid() in connectorState.js, never the raw field.

`labels` (string[]) appears on every file row — the use-case taxonomy written at upload time via connectors/upload's `labels`/`files_meta` fields (see api-data/cdm-connectors-upload.json). This is the read-back path for labels, which previously had none. The vocabulary itself is served by GET /connectors/labels, not hardcoded.

Timestamps here are ISO-8601 with a `T` separator and no timezone ('2026-08-14T09:19:50.128325'), whereas connectors/state uses a space separator for the same kind of field. Neither carries a zone designator — parse both with src/lib/time's parseUTC, never bare `new Date(str)` (bare parsing reads the space-separated form as LOCAL time and silently shifts the epoch by the viewer's UTC offset).

ERROR SHAPES ARE NOT UNIFORM on this router — three distinct families, and code that only handles one will mis-read the others. (1) App-level envelope: {success:false, message, errors:[{field, message}]} — used for every domain validation (bad flow, bad lifecycle, lifecycle/status conflict, bad connector, flowUid<=0, missing content_hash) and for 404s. (2) FastAPI auto-validation: {detail:[{type, loc, msg, input, ctx?}]} — used for a MISSING required query param and for an out-of-bounds one (page_size>1000). (3) Bare 401: {detail: "Missing session"} — a STRING, not an array. Note also that flowUid<=0 and a missing content_hash return 400, NOT 422, while the other envelope validations return 422.

endpoints.description: One row per file, newest first (sorted by updated_at). Drives the file grid, the button gating and the reprocess modal.

flow.values: aif | docs | gloc | lopc | pnid | sap | ts | ts_values — case-insensitive, trimmed, echoed back normalised. Blank string is a 422; a connector name is a 422.

status.note: Alias for lifecycle. Sending both with disagreeing values is a 422. The frontend does NOT expose this param at all — getFlowState only accepts `lifecycle`, which makes the conflict unrepresentable.

page_size.note: Out of range is a FastAPI-shaped 422 ({detail:[{type:'less_than_equal', loc:['query','page_size'], ctx:{le:1000}}]}), not the app envelope. The service clamps to this range before sending.

data.flow: string | null — echoes the requested flow, normalised; null when the param was omitted
data.lifecycle: string — echoes the effective lifecycle filter, 'all' when unset
data.status: string — echoes the deprecated alias, 'all' when unset
data.files: array of the 47-field row (see rowSchema below)

endpoints.sampleResponseNote: 2026-08-18 sample (PLANT_2): flow_uid 51, testfile.pdf, flow 'docs', file_type 'compressor_inspection', stage 'processed', status 'done', row_count 5, category 'others/compressor_inspection', duplicate_of 51 (ITS OWN uid — not a duplicate). pagination {page 1, page_size 2, total_items 30, total_pages 15, has_more true, next_cursor null}.
endpoints.verdict: MIGRATED 2026-08-18 — `status` param replaced by `lifecycle`; page/page_size now actively used by the paging loop; the eight-way fan-out collapsed to one call.
endpoints.serviceFn: getFlowState(plantCode, { flow, lifecycle, page, pageSize, signal }) and getAllFlowFiles(plantCode, { lifecycle, pageSize, signal }) in src/services/domain-configuration/common/connectorsService.js
endpoints.queryHooks: useFlowFilesQuery(plantCode, { lifecycle }) is the single shared read; useFlowFiles(plantCode) folds it into configuredSources entries; useFlowStateForFlow(plantCode, flow) (re-exported as useFlowState from useDsiQueries) slices ONE flow off the same payload. All three live in src/components/admin/_queries/useFlowFiles.js. Key: queryKeys.domainConfig.connector.flowState(plant, lifecycle).
endpoints.fetchStrategy: ONE request for the whole plant, paged. `flow` is omitted so every flow arrives together; getAllFlowFiles follows pagination.has_more with page_size 500 up to a hard stop of 40 pages (reported back as `truncated`). Per-flow slices are cut client-side by groupFilesByFlow. This REPLACED the previous lazy per-flow fan-out (BASELINE_FLOWS=['docs'] widened to all eight via a requestAllFlowFiles() call from DataConfigView) — that whole mechanism, including the context-exposed widener, was deleted. `lifecycle` stays a SERVER filter and is part of the query key, because the backend applies it before pagination; re-deriving it client-side over one page would disagree with the server as soon as a plant outgrows a page.

endpoints.description: One file's full row. Use after a reprocess or a commit to refresh a single grid row without re-fetching the list.

flowUid.values: any positive integer, taken from files[].flow_uid. <= 0 is rejected with 400.

responseShape.data: ⚠ THE ROW OBJECT DIRECTLY — NOT wrapped in files[]. Same 47 fields as a list row.

errors: 404 {success:false, message:'flow_uid not found', errors:[{field:'request', message:'flow_uid not found'}]}
400 (NOT 422) for flowUid <= 0: errors:[{field:'flowUid', message:'flowUid must be a positive integer'}]
endpoints.proxyRoute: src/app/api/domain-configuration/flow/state/[flowUid]/route.js (nested under the STATIC `state` segment, so it can never shadow /flow/[flowUid])
endpoints.queryHook: useFlowStateRow(plantCode, flowUid) in useDsiQueries.js — retry:false, since both failure modes (404, 400) are unfixable by retrying (rule 51). Key: queryKeys.domainConfig.connector.flowStateRow(plant, flowUid), under the shared flow-state prefix so flowStateAll invalidates rows too.

endpoints.description: Admin / recovery only. The backend maintains flow_state itself during a normal upload, so the UI should never need this — it exists to seed a row while testing.

_optional.note: Any settable column advances the row: file_name, file_type, size_bytes, stage, status, error, category, content_type, page_count, has_text_layer, sheet_names, labels, duplicate_of, uploaded_by, site, row_count, … `created_by` defaults to the authenticated actor.

endpoints.identity: (plant_code_id, flow, content_hash). Posting the same three again ADVANCES the same row rather than creating a second one — flow_uid is unchanged.
errors: 400 (NOT 422) {success:false, message:'Validation failed', errors:[{field:'content_hash', message:'content_hash cannot be empty'}]}
endpoints.verdict: NOT WIRED — deliberately. The backend owns flow_state during normal uploads, so exposing a client-side upsert would create a second, racing writer for rows the pipeline is already maintaining. Documented here so the capability is discoverable if a recovery/admin tool ever needs it.

endpoints.description: Reset a file to 'uploaded' so it can be reprocessed — the action behind the reprocess control. Sets stage='uploaded', status='pending', error=NULL, bumps attempt_count, and returns the updated row.

plant_code_id.note: ⚠ BODY here, but QUERY STRING for DELETE below. The two are genuinely inconsistent — this is the backend's own asymmetry, confirmed deliberate, not a transcription error.

responseShape.data: the updated row (same 47 fields); stage='uploaded', status='pending', error=null, attempt_count incremented

errors: 404 {success:false, message:'flow_uid not found', errors:[{field:'request', message:'flow_uid not found'}]}
endpoints.verdict: NEW — wired 2026-08-18. Note this is a PER-FILE reset, distinct from the existing per-SOURCE-TYPE reprocess, which goes through the pipeline's `force` flag (AdminProcessDataModal → runPipeline). The two coexist; neither replaces the other.
endpoints.queryHook: useResetFlowState(plantCode) in useDsiQueries.js — invalidates BOTH connector.flowStateAll(plant) and connector.state(plant), because a reset moves one file out of `processed` and into `pending` in the rollup's counts too.

endpoints.description: Remove a file from the flow entirely — the grid's row-delete action.

plant_code_id.note: ⚠ QUERY here, unlike the BODY placement on /reset above.

responseShape.data: { deleted: <flow_uid> } — the deleted id, NOT the row

errors: 404 {success:false, message:'flow_uid not found', errors:[{field:'request', message:'flow_uid not found'}]}
endpoints.queryHook: useDeleteFlowState(plantCode) in useDsiQueries.js — same invalidation pair as the reset.

flowCatalog.holds: Document files — inspection reports, manuals, drawings, procedures.
P&ID drawings and the entities extracted from them.
Time-series TAG DEFINITIONS — the sensor/tag master.
Time-series READINGS — the actual measurements. A SECOND flow under the same connector; this is why timeseries cannot be aliased to one flow.
SAP table extracts — equipment master, functional locations, notifications.

rowSchema._note: 47 fields. `⭐` marks the two ids that link a row to a pipeline run.
rowSchema.flow_uid: integer — PRIMARY KEY. The id passed to /flow/state/{flowUid}, /reset and DELETE. Use as the React key (rule 35); also what connectors/state's groups[].file_ids refers to.
rowSchema.plant_code_id: string — always echoes what you asked for.
rowSchema.site: string — sub-site within the plant. Currently always '-'; not populated yet.
rowSchema.flow: string — one of the eight flow names. Safe to group the grid by.
rowSchema.file_type: string — the subtype chosen at upload (e.g. compressor_inspection).
rowSchema.content_hash: string (sha256) — part of the row identity; duplicate detection uses it.
rowSchema.stage: string — WHERE in the pipeline. See the vocabularies note.
rowSchema.status: string — OUTCOME of the last operation. NOT the lifecycle filter.
rowSchema.error: string | null — failure text when status='failed'. Surface in the row's error tooltip.
rowSchema.hash_method: string | null — how content_hash was computed. Often null.
rowSchema.upload_job_id: uuid string — the upload job that created the row.
rowSchema.rustfs_path: string — object-store path of the raw file.
rowSchema.upload_batch_id: uuid string — ⭐ pass to /pipeline/run to scope a run to just this upload.
rowSchema.process_job_id: uuid string — ⭐ the pipeline job that processed it; poll /pipeline/jobs/{jobId} with this.
rowSchema.processed_parquet: string | null — object-store path of the extracted output.
rowSchema.row_count: integer | null — rows extracted from this file. null means NOT YET EXTRACTED, which is not the same as 0.
rowSchema.rows_in: integer | null — rows read before rejection.
rowSchema.rows_rejected: integer | null — rows dropped during extraction (rows_in minus row_count).
rowSchema.review_patches: integer | null — count of reviewer edits applied.
rowSchema.review_deletes: integer | null — count of reviewer deletes applied.
rowSchema.commit_uid: integer | null — the commit that wrote this file's rows to CDM.
rowSchema.rows_ingested: integer | null — rows landed in the canonical table.
rowSchema.iotdb_path: string | null — time-series storage path. ts / ts_values only.
rowSchema.ts_from: timestamp | null — earliest timestamp in the file. ts_values only.
rowSchema.ts_to: timestamp | null — latest timestamp in the file. ts_values only.
rowSchema.processing_started_at: ISO-8601 string | null — when the pipeline picked it up.
rowSchema.processed_at: ISO-8601 string | null — when extraction finished.
rowSchema.attempt_count: integer | null — processing attempts so far. Bumped by /reset.
rowSchema.category: string — taxonomy PATH, connector/group/subtype (e.g. 'others/compressor_inspection'). Groups the file grid; the frontend shows the leaf and keeps the full path as a title.
rowSchema.page_count: integer | null — PDF pages. null for spreadsheets.
rowSchema.has_text_layer: boolean | null — false means the PDF is a scan and needed OCR. Worth surfacing.
rowSchema.sheet_names: string[] | null — worksheet names for xlsx. null for PDFs.
rowSchema.labels: string[] | null — use-case labels chosen at upload: integrity | reliability | maintenance | production.
rowSchema.duplicate_of: integer | null — flow_uid of the file this duplicates. ⚠ CAN EQUAL ITS OWN flow_uid; see notes.
rowSchema.created_by: string | null — actor that created the row.
rowSchema.updated_at: ISO-8601 string — the list is sorted by this, newest first.

openIssues: `next_cursor` coexists with page/page_size and has only ever been observed as null. Unclear whether cursor pagination becomes authoritative past some page count; getAllFlowFiles uses page/page_size + has_more and ignores next_cursor.
No sample yet of a row in a FAILED state, so the populated shapes of `error`, `attempt_count` and `last_error_at` are still inferred rather than confirmed.
`stage='superseded'` has never been observed live. It is handled as pending (per the backend's derivation table) but the UI has no dedicated treatment for it.

Row `status` values `running`, `ok` and `skipped` have never been observed live. `ok` vs `done` in particular is undocumented — both appear to mean success, and the frontend treats anything that is not 'failed' as non-failing, which is safe for both.
POST /flow/upsert is intentionally not wired (see its verdict). If a recovery tool ever needs it, the open question is what should own writes to a table the pipeline is concurrently maintaining.
